versions.changelog:
push-server v1.6.3

- Expanded descriptions to highlight support for registration-free personal channel onboarding using create_auth_session + poll_auth_session (Gitee, GitHub, Feishu, DingTalk login).
- Clarified workflow and rules for onboarding a channel without account registration.
- Removed sample file (skill-card.md) for a leaner package.
- No changes to API or core functionality; documentation improved for onboarding and credential flow.

Version 1.6.0

- Added support for two new tools (`create_auth_session` and `poll_auth_session`) to enable "no-register" channel creation for users without a pre-existing channel code.
- Updated documentation to cover the new no-registration channel-creation flow, including how to initiate and complete the auth session and related security considerations.
- Clarified tool division: now explicitly notes five available MCP tools (previously three).
- Detailed the logic for user credential handling and tool selection accordingly.

push-server 1.5.4

- Documented pushUrl / qrCodeUrl usage (share/manage page and mobile push-records QR) and fixed the ping self-check response example.

push-server 1.5.1

- Removed the sample file skill-card.md.
- No changes to core functionality or logic.

push-server 1.5.0

- Major update: Adds multi-message batching and message query features, refactors documentation structure, and introduces new reference files.
- Introduced `send_multi_message` for batch sending—each from a separate source, with optional per-message channel codes.
- Added support for reading back message history and managing channels using OAuth2 HTTP APIs (`get_access_token` + `/oauth2/push/*` endpoints).
- Documentation split: two new references (`references/api.md`, `references/example.md`) provide detailed API specs and practical message examples.
- Expanded usage guidelines on emoji formatting, batch vs. single push, and direct links to reference materials.
- Removed `.gitignore` and old skill card; all key technical and user instructions now consolidated and updated.

Initial release of push-server skill.

- Enables sending push notifications (head + Markdown/JSON body, optional jump link) to users via the push server MCP.
- Supports notifications to IM clients, browsers, or webhook APIs; structured content can be pushed to business servers.
- Includes detailed setup instructions for channel code configuration and MCP server integration.
- Enforces strict security: user-provided channel code only, sensitive data must be masked.
- Provides Markdown/JSON formatting rules and mandatory URL cleaning to ensure message readability and link accessibility.
- Clear success/failure handling and user guidance included.
